strengths: Principled and well-motivated formulation: Instead of relying purely on heuristic agentic pipelines and external prompt scaffolding, the paper formulates scientific ideation as motivation-grounded multi-stage reasoning (context -> motivation -> reasoning -> methodology) and trains an open-source model (14B) to internalize the deduction process.

Innovative composite reward mechanism: The combination of micro-level Entropy-Aware Information Gain (EAIG)—which focuses reward credit on dense, high-information technical concepts rather than boilerplate phrases—and macro-level Contrastive Semantic Gain (CSG) effectively steers open-ended reasoning toward substantive solutions without deterministic verifiers.

Rigorous treatment of optimization dynamics: The authors provide both empirical ablations and formal theoretical analysis regarding GRPO's implicit variance aversion and reasoning length collapse, presenting Length Anchoring as an effective stabilizer.

Comprehensive evaluation and human validation: The proposed method is evaluated against strong commercial models (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) and multi-agent systems across both in-domain (ICLR) and out-of-domain (NeurIPS) benchmarks, supported by human expert validation demonstrating solid correlation with the LLM judge (Pearson r = 0.715).
weaknesses: Ground-truth dependence during RL training: Both EAIG and CSG require comparing rollouts against a specific historical ground-truth paper (y*). While this functions as a training surrogate, scientific ideation is fundamentally open-ended with many valid orthogonal solutions; optimizing primarily against a single historical target may penalize valid alternative hypotheses during training.

Domain specificity: The empirical benchmarks are confined solely to machine learning / AI conference papers (ICLR and NeurIPS). It remains an open question whether this reasoning paradigm transfers seamlessly to broader scientific disciplines (e.g., life sciences, physical sciences, or empirical linguistic field studies) where methodology structure differs significantly.

Marginal difference compared to top proprietary foundation models: While MoRI (14B) substantially outperforms agentic baselines and GPT-4o, its overall score difference over prompting Claude-3.5-Sonnet is modest (3.18 vs. 3.11) and not statistically significant in pairwise testing, with Claude maintaining higher novelty scores.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated conceptual framing: Instead of relying on complex external agentic scaffolding (e.g., multi-agent debate, search loops), MoRI demonstrates that scientific ideation can be internalized directly into LLM reasoning via motivation-grounded reinforcement learning.

Principled reward design for open-ended generation: The dual-granularity composite reward—combining micro-level Entropy-Aware Information Gain (targeting informative technical tokens) with macro-level Contrastive Semantic Gain (penalizing mere regurgitation of input context) and length anchoring—effectively tackles reward hacking and CoT collapse under GRPO.

Rigorous evaluation methodology: Evaluating open-ended ideation is challenging; the authors address this by pairing retrieval-grounded LLM evaluation with a blind human validation study involving three ML PhD annotators, establishing respectable correlation (Pearson r = 0.715) and inter-annotator agreement (ICC = 0.695).

Comprehensive empirical analysis: The submission provides thorough comparisons across both in-domain (ICLR) and out-of-domain (NeurIPS) benchmarks, outperforming full-SFT baselines and multi-agent systems, supported by rigorous ablation studies, bootstrap confidence intervals, and significance testing.
weaknesses: Dependence on reference targets during RL: Both EAIG and CSG rely on the existence of a specific historical ground-truth method section y*. In real-world scientific discovery, a research context can branch into numerous equally valid yet divergent methodologies; rewarding convergence toward a single historical paper during exploration may penalize viable, creative alternatives.

Evaluation remains purely textual: While feasibility and technical rigor are evaluated by human experts and retrieval-augmented judges, none of the generated ideas are validated via downstream implementation, experimentation, or code execution, leaving practical realizability partially unverified.

Limited domain diversity: Experiments are confined strictly to machine learning publications (ICLR and NeurIPS). Scientific ideation in experimental sciences (e.g., chemistry, wet-lab biology, materials science) involves different evidentiary standards and logical workflows that are not addressed.

Competitive parity with leading proprietary frontier models: Although MoRI uses a substantially smaller open-weight backbone (14B), its overall performance gain over Claude-3.5-Sonnet is not statistically significant (p = n.s. after Bonferroni correction), and Claude retains an advantage in the Novelty dimension.

strengths: Novel and principled formulation of scientific ideation as a motivation-grounded reasoning process (Context -> Motivation -> Reasoning -> Methodology), shifting the focus from external agentic scaffolding to internalizing reasoning capabilities within the model weights.

Well-designed composite reward function combining micro-level Entropy-Aware Information Gain (EAIG) on substantive technical tokens with macro-level Contrastive Semantic Gain (CSG), effectively circumventing the lack of deterministic ground-truth verifiers in open-ended scientific generation.

Comprehensive empirical analysis and ablation studies demonstrating the necessity of each component (e.g., motivation conditioning, length anchoring, entropy filtering), backed by an insightful theoretical explanation of length collapse under GRPO in Appendix F.

Rigorous evaluation methodology featuring a retrieval-augmented LLM judge that correlates well with blind human expert evaluations (Pearson r = 0.715), along with extensive statistical significance testing (bootstrap CIs and Bonferroni-corrected t-tests).
weaknesses: The training reward relies on a single ground-truth methodology ($y^*$). In open-ended scientific discovery, multiple fundamentally distinct methodological directions could be valid and novel for a given context; penalizing divergence from the specific historical paper via token log-likelihood and semantic proximity may constrain open-ended exploration during RL.

Evaluation and dataset are restricted entirely to machine learning publications (ICLR and NeurIPS), leaving open the question of whether the motivation-to-methodology reasoning paradigm transfers to disciplines with different publication and formalization norms (e.g., natural sciences or biomedical research).

Although MoRI outperforms agentic systems and GPT-4o, the overall performance gap over strong commercial baselines like Claude-3.5-Sonnet is narrow and statistically non-significant on the combined set (with Claude still outperforming MoRI on Novelty).

strengths: The paper introduces a principled formulation of scientific ideation as motivation-grounded reasoning, internalizing the ideation process via reinforcement learning rather than relying solely on external multi-agent scaffolding or naive supervised imitation.

The composite reward framework is well-motivated: pairing Entropy-Aware Information Gain (EAIG) on core technical tokens with Contrastive Semantic Gain (CSG) effectively balances micro-level technical depth and macro-level conceptual progress.

The theoretical and empirical analysis of length bias in GRPO (Appendix F and Section 4.3) is insightful, explaining the mechanism behind reasoning chain collapse under reward variance and justifying the length-anchoring penalty.

The evaluation is thorough, including comparisons against frontier models (Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-4o), specialized agentic frameworks (AI-Scientist-V2, ResearchAgent, VirSci), and ablation variants, complemented by blind human expert validation demonstrating strong correlation (r = 0.715) with the LLM judge.
weaknesses: The training rewards (EAIG and CSG) strongly rely on reconstructing a single ground-truth reference paper methodology (y*). Because scientific discovery is inherently open-ended with many valid solutions for a given motivation, conditioning optimization on a single target may penalize valid alternative solutions and limit open-ended creative exploration.

The test suite consists of 83 holdout papers and human validation is conducted over a relatively small sample (60 total instances, with only 15 per system), which limits the statistical power of the human assessment.

The dataset creation relies on 'Qwen3-235B-Instruct' and 'Qwen3-235B-Thinking' for posterior reconstruction and extraction; clarification on model accessibility, replication details, or open alternatives is necessary to guarantee reproducibility.

strengths: Conceptual shift from agentic scaffolding to internalized reasoning: The paper presents an appealing formulation of scientific ideation as a two-stage reasoning process (context to motivation, and motivation to method), training the model parameters directly via RL rather than relying on complex external agent loops.

Principled surrogate reward design for unverified domains: The dual-granularity reward framework—combining Entropy-Aware Information Gain (EAIG) on informative ground-truth tokens with Contrastive Semantic Gain (CSG) and length-anchoring regularization—provides a creative and effective surrogate for scientific rigor in open-ended reasoning tasks without deterministic verifiers.

Thorough ablations and training dynamics analysis: The paper includes rigorous ablations (Table 3, 4, 5) and detailed training curves (Figures 3, 4, 5) dissecting the failure modes of individual components (e.g., reward collapse and gibberish when using EAIG alone, reasoning chain collapse without length anchoring), effectively illuminating the optimization mechanics.

Rigorous evaluation with human alignment: The evaluation framework is thorough, combining retrieval-augmented LLM judging with a blind human evaluation across 60 instances by machine learning researchers, showing solid Pearson correlation (r = 0.715).
weaknesses: Conceptual tension in reward design: Both EAIG and CSG rely heavily on alignment with a single ground-truth methodology (y*). Because scientific discovery is inherently open-ended and one-to-many, penalizing valid divergent ideas that deviate from the specific historical publication's solution could inadvertently train the model toward retrospective reconstruction rather than genuine open-ended ideation.

Narrow domain and evaluation scope: The evaluation is conducted entirely on 83 papers from a single domain (machine learning, ICLR 2025). The feasibility and technical rigor of the proposed ideas are judged purely on the generated text descriptions without downstream empirical execution or code implementation.

Modest margins over commercial zero-shot/few-shot baselines: While MoRI (14B) demonstrates a strong improvement over its direct SFT baseline and agentic frameworks, the overall score margin over Claude-3.5-Sonnet is modest (3.19 vs. 3.09, +3.2%), and Claude-3.5-Sonnet still achieves higher raw Novelty (3.39 vs. 3.31).

Synthetic data quality in posterior reconstruction: The initial reasoning chains (z) used for cold-start SFT are synthesized via posterior reconstruction using proprietary LLMs (Qwen-235B). The paper lacks a quantitative analysis of whether these reverse-engineered thought traces introduce post-hoc rationalization biases or artifacts into the policy initialization.

strengths: Principled and well-structured formulation of scientific ideation, decomposing the generation pipeline into motivation extraction, internal reasoning trajectory, and detailed methodology synthesis.

Novel composite surrogate reward design for non-verifiable open-ended generation: combining microscopic Entropy-Aware Information Gain (EAIG) on informative tokens with macroscopic Contrastive Semantic Gain (CSG) and length anchoring.

Comprehensive empirical analysis and ablation studies that thoroughly examine reward dynamics, revealing why isolated rewards cause collapse or superficial hacking and highlighting the necessity of length regularization.

Strong experimental comparisons spanning leading frontier models (GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) and multi-agent scientific discovery frameworks (AI-Scientist-V2, ResearchAgent, VirSci), complemented by human correlation validation.
weaknesses: The training rewards (EAIG and CSG) strictly measure alignment with the specific ground-truth paper's method ($y^*$). In scientific ideation, multiple distinct, equally valid, or even more creative methodologies could arise from the same research context; penalizing divergence from the historical ground truth biases the policy toward reverse-engineering existing papers rather than open-ended discovery.

The evaluation set is relatively modest, comprising only 83 holdout papers from ICLR 2025, and human evaluation is limited to 60 samples (15 per system across 4 systems), which somewhat restricts the statistical power and broad generalizability of the findings.

The scope is currently confined entirely to machine learning publications (ICLR); it remains an open question whether the motivation-to-methodology reasoning patterns learned here transfer to empirical sciences (e.g., biology, chemistry, physics) with differing epistemological paradigms.
